source_note: Structural/topical citations from NAVSEA S0570-AC-CCM-010/8010, 'Industrial Ship Safety Manual for Fire Prevention and Response,' Distribution Statement A (approved for public release, distribution unlimited), dated 06 Feb 2014, smoothed version 26 Aug 2014, hosted at NAVSEA's own FOIA reading room. This is a SITE-SCOPED ruleset -- installation='PSNS' -- not a universal Navy-wide source. A different installation/command (NASNI, NAVSTA Everett, SURFPAC vs AIRPAC vs AIRLANT, etc.) may operate under different governing instructions; this file should not be treated as applicable outside the installation it's tagged for. Only HOT_WORK is covered -- this manual does not address confined_space, working_aloft, fall_protection, or over_the_side at all, so no entries exist for those categories and none should be added here (see case_data/cases_v1.json for those).
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: APPROVED FOR PUBLIC RELEASE; DISTRIBUTION IS UNLIMITED
verification_note: Section titles and topical scope were extracted via automated document fetch, not a verbatim primary-source read. 'summary' fields below are accurate to that structural extraction. Any field marked verified=false has NOT been confirmed against the primary-source PDF text for exact numeric/procedural specifics (counts, distances, durations) and must not be treated as a citable exact requirement until someone reads the actual section and confirms it.

procedures.summary: Hot work requires written authorization before commencing: written notice, designated signing authority approval, posting of the notice at the work site, and notification to the Commanding Officer's representative.

procedures.section: Chapter 4.3 - Gas-Free Procedures and Special Hazards
procedures.summary: Hot work is governed by gas-free testing procedures; certain compartments/spaces are restricted from hot work; protective coverings, precautions around lines/piping carrying flammable or combustible fluids, proximity controls around flammables/combustibles, restrictions near ammunition/explosives, and special precautions for battery-charging areas all apply.

procedures.section: Chapter 4.4.3 - Limitations to Single Fire Watch with Multiple Hot Workers
procedures.summary: A single fire watch cannot supervise unlimited concurrent hot work activity -- the manual places a limitation on how many hot workers one fire watch can cover at once. Exact numeric limit not confirmed against primary text.

procedures.section: Chapter 4.4.4 - Hot Work Involving Multiple Levels
procedures.summary: Hot work spanning multiple deck levels requires enhanced fire watch protocols beyond a single-level assignment.
Hot work performed in a compartment not directly observable by the fire watch (a 'blind compartment') requires special fire watch provisions beyond standard line-of-sight supervision.

Fire zone boundaries must be maintained and marked; temporary access cuts through fire zone boundaries during industrial work are permitted under controlled conditions and must be recorded (audit trail of boundary openings); boundaries may be temporarily degraded during maintenance and must be tracked as such.

procedures.section: Chapter 11.1.7 - Boundaries on Carrier Type Ships
procedures.summary: Special fire zone boundary provisions apply specifically to aircraft carrier-type ships, distinct from the general fire zone boundary rules elsewhere in Chapter 11.
